name: Taskip
tagline: White-label client portal and agency workspace with CRM, projects, invoicing and payments
summary: Taskip is a hosted workspace for agencies, freelancers and service businesses. It has task boards with Kanban, list, Gantt and calendar views, a client portal where clients follow progress, sign documents, share files, open tickets and pay invoices, team discussions, a WhatsApp and email inbox, branded quotes and invoices, a CRM pipeline, timers and timesheets. Payments go through Stripe, PayPal and other gateways. A built-in AI agent drafts replies and creates invoices, and an MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor work in a workspace. Web, iOS and Android apps.
watching: It was named in a 2026-10-27 X thread asking for one platform for agency client work. It covers the same tasks, chat and CRM ground as the desktop's Tasks, Chat and CRM packages, adds the client portal and invoicing ForkMesh does not have, and exposes its workspace to agents over MCP as ForkMesh does.

comparison.forkmesh: An open-source network for hosting, mirroring and collaborating on Git repositories, with coding agents as one part of its desktop app.

name: Loftside
tagline: Client portal for agencies and freelancers where clients get a private link, not an account
summary: Loftside is an early, unlaunched client portal for agencies and freelancers. Each client gets a private magic link to a page in the studio's name and colour showing work in progress, what is due, what they owe and the latest message, with no account or password. Project boards mark every task as visible to the client or private, chat and files sit beside the work, and invoices with line items, tax and due dates print to PDF and will be paid by card through Stripe. Teammates have owner, admin and member roles, and members never see money. Planned from $19 a month per studio.

name: Daily Tracker
tagline: Shared daily work log for small teams with routines, live timers and a daily completion score
summary: Daily Tracker is a hosted daily work log for small teams. Routines appear on the days they are scheduled, tasks carry timers that bank time on pause and keep it across a closed laptop, subtasks rebuild each scheduled day with their own clocks, and each day closes with one completion figure counted against what was scheduled. Everyone in a workspace reads the same day; owners write and members propose work for an owner to approve or reject.
